name: Solar Project Benchmarking
tagline: An on-premises platform for outside-in CapEx and schedule benchmarking of utility-scale solar PV projects.
problem: Consultants benchmarking a solar project's cost and schedule have to find comparable projects, pull defensible numbers from scattered public sources and normalize them before any comparison is fair. This platform is built to plan that research, score source credibility, normalize costs for time, currency and location, and then model CapEx and schedule against the reference class. It targets management consultants working in restricted corporate environments.
how: Create a project with its name, asset type, location and capacity in the web UI; it is stored through the FastAPI projects API.
The research planner turns the project into a query plan: search queries with capacity variants, target domains, must-include and exclude terms, and crawl heuristics.
The research service crawls allowed sources, extracts facts and scores each source's credibility.
The normalization service adjusts comparator costs to a base quarter and currency and flags conflicts between sources.
CapEx (parametric fit, variance waterfall, levers) and schedule (CPM, Monte Carlo, RCPSP) endpoints are defined as the modeling layer.
features: Dashboard with project counts, database type read from the API and an API health indicator
Create, list and soft-delete projects, with creation dates shown in the list
Research query planner generating search queries and target domains per project
Credibility scoring and conflict detection services
Time, currency and location normalization service
Interactive Swagger and ReDoc API documentation
Database schema covering sources, extracts, comparators, CapEx models, schedules, Monte Carlo runs, exports and audit logs
API base URL configurable with a ?api= query parameter on the page
ai: No LLM is used. Research planning, credibility scoring and normalization are rule-based Python services.
The CapEx modeling and schedule analytics endpoints currently return placeholder values in this repo.

stack.frontend: Single-file Vue 3 page with Tailwind CSS
stack.data: SQLite by default (portable UUID type); PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL, with db/schema.sql for Postgres
stack.deploy: Local uvicorn server; frontend opened as a static file

run:
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r api/requirements.txt
cd api && uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
# then open frontend/index.html in a browser (add ?api=http://127.0.0.1:PORT to use another API port)
notes: The app now runs from the repo with its default SQLite database and no local PostgreSQL. Fixes committed in the local repo (not pushed): the models use SQLAlchemy's portable Uuid type instead of the PostgreSQL-only UUID, so tables are created on SQLite; the project list response now includes created_at and updated_at, so the Created column shows real dates instead of Invalid Date; /health reports the database type and the dashboard Database card shows it instead of a hardcoded SQLite label; the frontend API base URL can be set with ?api= instead of being fixed to port 8000; db/schema.sql was synced to the models (project_metadata column, JSONB lists instead of arrays, VARCHAR ip_address, NOT NULL foreign keys) and was loaded successfully into PostgreSQL 16 as a check; pytest was pinned to 7.4.4 because the requirements file could not resolve. Caveats: the frontend still loads Vue and Tailwind from CDNs, which are blocked in the capture environment, so during capture the browser was served the same Vue 3 build and a compiled Tailwind v3 stylesheet from npm (and Swagger UI assets from npm) with no change to the repo. The CapEx (parametric fit, variance, levers), schedule (CPM, Monte Carlo, RCPSP) and export endpoints are stubs that return fixed placeholder values; they were left as is and are not shown as results. The research planner is a real rule-based service; crawling was not run because it needs outbound web access. The three projects were typed into the real form as example inputs. No LLM is involved.
